questions.q: What is the core idea of infrastructure as code, unchanged whether the target is an app server or a SQL Server instance?
options: You write an imperative step-by-step script that must be run manually every time
A declarative file describes the desired end state, is kept in version control, and a tool reconciles reality to match it
Infrastructure is described only in a wiki page, never in a file a tool can read
IaC only applies to cloud resources, never to on-premises servers
questions.explain: That declarative, version-controlled, tool-applied shape is the same whether you're standing up an app server or a SQL Server instance.

questions.q: In this lesson's terms, what does 'provisioning' mean?
options: Setting sp_configure values on an already-running instance
Bringing a compute/storage/networking resource into existence, such as the VM or the Azure SQL Database resource itself
Writing a maintenance job schedule
Creating SQL logins and permissions
questions.explain: Provisioning is about the resource existing at all — the compute, storage, and networking it needs.

questions.q: In this lesson's terms, what does 'configuration' mean?
options: Setting the state of what's running on a resource once it exists — memory limits, sp_configure values, logins, jobs
Deleting a resource that is no longer needed
Naming a resource group in the cloud provider's console
Choosing which region a VM will be deployed to
questions.explain: Configuration is what happens after the resource exists — the SQL-Server-specific internal state.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say IaC tools model SQL Server configuration poorly compared to provisioning?
options: Configuration is against Microsoft's licensing terms to automate
SQL Server configuration cannot be automated by any tool, ever
IaC tools are built primarily to describe infrastructure resources, not the fine-grained internal state of a running SQL Server instance like specific logins or sp_configure values
IaC tools are only compatible with Linux servers
questions.explain: IaC tools like Terraform and Bicep excel at declaring resources to exist; SQL Server internals are typically handled by a separate configuration step.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what real benefit does an IaC definition give you that a written runbook does not, in a disaster-recovery scenario?
options: IaC guarantees zero downtime during any rebuild
IaC eliminates the need for backups entirely
IaC definitions automatically back up all data inside the database
The IaC definition is the actual, automatically-applied recipe to rebuild the server, rather than a document that may be stale or never re-validated
questions.explain: A runbook can silently go stale; an IaC template that's actually applied by a tool reflects what the infrastructure is meant to be right now.
